statement.p: At a certain point on a heated metal plate, the greatest rate of temperature increase, 4 degrees Celsius per meter, is toward the northeast. If an object at this point moves directly north, at what rate is the temperature increasing?

solution.p: Let T be the temperature function and P the point. The value of the greatest rate of increase is the magnitude of the gradient. Thus \left| \nabla T (P) \right| = 4.
The gradient points in the northeast direction, so \nabla T (P) = \left \langle 4 \cos (45^o) , 4 \sin (45^o) \right \rangle = \left \langle \frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{4}{\sqrt{2}} \right \rangle.

A unit vector in the north direction is \mathbf{u} = \langle 0, 1 \rangle, so the rate of change of increase of the temperature in that direction is D_{\mathbf u} T(P) = \nabla T (P) \cdot \mathbf{u} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}
